sentences.text: CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S. INDIRESH  ORAL ORDER

In this writ petition, the petitioners are seeking writ of mandamus against the respondents to issue the necessary Development Right Certificate in lieu of acquisition of subject land belonging to the petitioners by extending the benefit under the provisions of Section 14-B of Karnataka Town and Country Planning (Amendment) Act, 2021 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'KTCP (Amendment)
Act-2021').

entities.text: Karnataka Town and Country Planning (Amendment) Act, 2021
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The facts leading to filing of this writ petition are that, late M. Krishna Reddy, husband of the petitioner No.1 and father of the petitioner No.2 claims to be the owner of the land bearing Survey No.150/1 of Agara Village, Bengaluru South Taluk measuring to an extent of 2 acre 1 gunta, having acquired the same in the partition deed dated 22nd February, 1965 and accordingly, the revenue records stands in the name of late M. Krishna Reddy.

It is stated in the writ petition that NC:
2024:KHC:50517 WP NO.24195 OF 2021 the respondent-Authorities have initiated acquisition proceedings for the purpose of formation of H.S.R. Layout and as such, issued Preliminary Notification dated 15th December, 1984 (Annexure-C) and Final Notification dated 28th November,
1986 (Annexure-D).

The said late M. Krishna Reddy has filed objections, opposing the acquisition of subject land and as such, the Special Land Acquisition Officer submitted report dated 13th February,
1989 (Annexure-E), which reveals that, the houses are constructed in the subject land and same is not viable for acquisition.

On perusal of Endorsement dated 31st March, 2016 (Annexure-F), the same would indicate that, award has not been passed and the respondent-Authorities have not taken possession in furtherance of the issuance of impugned notifications for acquisition.

It is also stated in the writ petition that the respondent-Bangalore Development Authority had interfered with the property in question in the guise of formation of Link Road in H.S.R. Layout and accordingly,
portion of the subject land was acquired for the purpose of Link Road.

It is also stated in the writ petition that late M. Krishna Reddy has made representations at Annexure-J series, seeking allotment of developed area for having acquired NC: 2024:KHC:50517 WP NO.24195 OF 2021 the land in question and the respondent No.3 vide resolution No.159/2018 (Annexure-K) had taken decision to issue Development Right Certificate to the land loosers.

In that view of the matter, the petitioners have sought for issuance of Development Right Certificate in lieu of acquisition of subject land and accordingly, joint survey was conducted as per Annexures 'L' and 'M' to the writ petition.

It is stated in the petition that, late M. Krishna Reddy has made a representation seeking benefit of Section 14-B of the 'KTCP (Amendment) Act- 2021 and same has not been considered by the respondent- Bangalore Development Authority.
Hence, this writ petition.

3. Heard Smt. S. Susheela, learned Senior Counsel on behalf of Sri. Shivaraju M.K., appearing for petitioners; Smt. Rashmi M. Rao, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondents 1 and 2; and Sri. Sachin B.S., learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3.

sentences.text:
Smt. S. Susheela, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that, though the land belonging to the petitioners has been acquired by the respondent-Authorities to form Link Road in H.S.R. Layout, neither award has been NC: 2024:KHC:50517 WP NO.24195 OF 2021 passed nor compensation is paid and possession of the subject land has been taken from the petitioners and therefore, in view of the resolution No.159/2018 (Annexure-K), the respondent- Bangalore Development Authority is bound to issue Development Right Certificate in favour of petitioners in terms of Section 14-B of the 'KTCP (Amendment) Act-2021.
5.

Per contra, Sri. B.S. Sachin, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Bangalore Development Authority submits that, neither the impugned acquisition proceedings has been quashed by this Court nor land in question has been de- notified, however, portion of the land belonging to the petitioners is utilised for formation of Road as well as Site and thereby, no award is passed.

It is further contended by learned counsel that the Development Right Certificate would be given to the land owners, if the land is utilised for public purpose and therefore, as the portion of the land is utilised for formation of Road, the claim made by the petitioners is contrary to Section 14-B of the KTCP (Amendment) Act-2021 and accordingly, sought for dismissal of the writ petition.
Smt. Rashmi M. Rao, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent No.1 argued on similar lines with the respondent-Bangalore Development Authority.

7. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that the portion of the land belonging to petitioners has been acquired by the respondents pursuant to the issuance of Preliminary Notification dated 15th December, 1984 and Final Notification dated 28th November, 1986 as per Annexures 'C' and 'D' respectively.
It is reflected in the report of Special Land Acquisition Officer produced at Annexure-E that, the houses have been built in the subject land.

It is also not in dispute that the portion of the land has been acquired for the purpose of formation of Link Road in H.S.R. Layout and further, no award has been passed by the respondent-Authorities.
It is also to be noted that the portion of land has been utilised and remaining land which is un-utilised is remained with the petitioners.

In that view of the matter, in view of Section 14-B of KTCP (Amendment) Act-2021, the petitioners are eligible for Development Right Certificate since, the area is surrendered to NC: 2024:KHC:50517 WP NO.24195 OF 2021 the respondent-Bangalore Development Authority as submitted by learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners.

8. Taking into consideration the fact that, the land in question has been acquired by the respondent-Authorities for the purpose of formation of Link Road, in view of law declared by this Court in the case of SRI. H.V. TEJAS AND ANOTHER vs. THE BRUHAT BENGALURU MAHANAGARA PALIKE made in Writ Petition No.10272 of 2020 decided of on 19th September,
2022, wherein, under similar circumstance, this Court has directed the respondents therein, not to deny the issuance of the Transferable Development Rights in respect of the schedule property therein and further, the aforementioned order in Writ Petition No.10272 of 2020 has been confirmed by the Division Bench of this Court in Writ Appeal No.1061 of 2022, disposed of on 10th M Krishna Reddy vs State Of Karnataka on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101756284/
4 November, 2022, I am of the view that as the petitioners are similarly placed and as such, the writ petition deserves to be allowed.
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also to be noted that, as the land belonging to the petitioners has been acquired for the purpose of formation of Link Road and if the Development Right Certificate is not NC:
2024:KHC:50517 WP NO.24195 OF 2021 issued in lieu of compensation, the same will curtail the Constitutional Right of the petitioners under Article 300-A of Constitution of India and also as per resolution No.159/2018 dated 15th December, 2018 (Annexure-K).

Therefore, taking into consideration the factual aspects on record, I find force in the submission made by the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners that the respondent-Authorities being an instrumentality of the State, have to issue the Development Right Certificate in respect of the subject land, having acquired the same for the purpose of formation of Link Road, which is further public purpose only.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER 1. Writ petition is allowed.
2. Writ of mandamus is issued to respondent No.3 to issue Development Right Certificate in lieu of compensation in respect of the land bearing Survey No.150/1 measuring 31 guntas out of 2 acre 1 gunta situate at Agara Village, Bengaluru South Taluk, within an outer limit of two months from the receipt of this order.

SD/-
